chief_complaint: Management of type 2 diabetes mellitus with associated metabolic syndrome (hypertension, obesity, dyslipidemia)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes diagnosed in May 2020 (most recent A1c 6.7%), essential hypertension diagnosed in May 2021, hypertriglyceridemia, obesity (BMI ≥30 since 1983) and metabolic syndrome. He is on metformin 500 mg ER daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Recent visits have focused on preventive care, including serial retinal photography for diabetic eye screening. No recent blood pressure, lipid panel, renal function, or BMI measurements are available. The current medication regimen appears sub‑optimally dosed (low‑dose metformin, no statin or additional glucose‑lowering agents) and there are gaps in risk‑modifying therapy despite high cardiovascular risk.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include viral sinusitis (2022), acute viral pharyngitis (2022), colon polyp (2022), prior reports of environmental violence (2021), previous full‑time employment (2021), social isolation (2019), and two lacerations of the thigh (2016). Medication review due entries from 2017 and 2019 have also resolved.
